Huh? "Wounded a Mandalay Bay security guard outside his door and sprayed 200 bullets down the hall" ... In a hotel like Mandalay? Why was nobody else hit? The walls must be bullet proof...

You'd probably be surprised then on how ineffective spraying bullets around is in reality. In the military we use machine guns for hitting a moving target we can see, or laying down suppressive fire. But not for situations like this, because it doesn't work like in the movies.

Let's say you have a human sized target behind a wall in a 20 meter long hallway. You have a magazine/belt with 200 rounds. So on average, you are going to have an average spread of 10 rounds per meter, which on the face of it, would seem like it would hit something. But, spreads generally don't work like that. For one thing, it's not likely that the target is right up against the wall. If you are firing from a fixed location there is going to be a radiant to the pattern. So, if the target is 10 meters behind the wall in the next room, the spread becomes more like 1 per meter on average. And a target at the end of the hall (10 meters down) and 10 meters behind the wall is going to have something like 1 bullet per 14 meters. Math is kind of crappy here. It's back of the napkin. But in general it should give you an idea of scale.

Then, consider, spray patterns aren't going to be consistent. There are going to be groupings, especially in the part of the wall that is directly in front of the shooter. So, (I don't have the math on this, but quick guesstimation), 50% of the rounds are going in the area almost directly in front of the shooter as opposed to the extremes of his spray. So, if the target happens to be almost in front of the shooter, he's probably fucked. But, most of the area is statistically "safe".

As we have found out though. Randomly spraying bullets is quite effective when you have thousands of targets standing around in an open area.
